title: Shakai: Who Said to the World “Enough”
summary: The ten things the world was created with, from chochmah and tevunah to chesed and rachamim. The world kept expanding like a ball of thread rolling off a loom until Hashem said "Dai," which is why He is called Shakai. Then whether heaven or earth came first, Rabbi Akiva on what he learned from Nachum Ish Gamzu, what the world stands on, the tzaddik as the foundation of the world, and the seven heavens.
key_ideas: Hashem holds the world in check at every moment, saying "enough" so it doesn't stretch too far from Him.
The world is left unfinished on purpose, so that people complete it, just as a child is born without a bris.
The world stands on the tzaddik, the people who connect it to Hashem.
One who learns Torah at night is granted chesed by day.
